newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese army in Hong Kong ducks poultry gifts.
newsitem.headline: Chinese army in Hong Kong ducks poultry gifts.

text.p: A group of Hong Kong children arrived at the headquarters of the Chinese army garrison on Friday bearing gifts of live chickens and ducks but were politely turned away at the gates.
The group, dressed in worn army fatigues, had brought along the gifts, including a huge basket of fresh eggs, to celebrate the 70th anniversary of China's People's Liberation Army (PLA).
But an army officer at the barracks in Hong Kong's bustling Central district refused the offer.
"We are very touched by the gesture. But we have our rules and we cannot accept your gifts," he told the group.
With chickens, ducks and geese tucked under their arms as they walked off, retired soldier and leader of the group Peter Chan expressed his displeasure.
"I'm very disappointed, very upset. What am I going to do with all these chickens and ducks now?" he told reporters.
Hong Kong, a British colony for 156 years, was reabsorbed by China on July 1. The PLA has kept a low profile here since its arrival.
